author: Good Enough
description:
Cauterization was one of the most terrifying treatments used in medieval medicine. Medieval barber-surgeons sometimes treated severe wounds by applying extreme heat or a heated iron to tissue in an attempt to stop bleeding and seal the injury.

Long before modern surgery, anesthesia, and antibiotics, cauterization could be used when a wound would not stop bleeding or when surgeons believed burning the area might prevent further complications. The treatment was intensely painful and could carry serious risks, but in some situations it was used as a last-resort method to control hemorrhaging.

This Short explores medieval cauterization, barber-surgeons, wound treatment, medieval surgery, and the brutal reality of medicine during the Middle Ages.
